images.title: One tiger picture in five sizes
images.purpose: Shows one tiger picture resized into five copies: three keep the look of the tiger, one is stretched and one is squashed.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Five rectangular picture frames stand in one row on a common baseline, each holding the same simple flat tiger face.
images.exact_structure: Exactly five rectangular frames with dark outlines in one row, bottoms on the same invisible baseline, evenly spaced, left to right A, B, C, D, E. Frame sizes in the same units: A 60 wide by 40 high, B 40 wide by 20 high, C 30 wide by 20 high, D 90 wide by 60 high, E 60 wide by 60 high. Inside every frame the same simple flat tiger face in amber (#E69F00) with dark stripes fills the frame: in A, C and D it has its natural proportions; in B it is stretched sideways so it looks long and thin; in E it is squeezed so it looks short and fat. Under each frame its single capital letter. Under A, C and D a small green (#009E73) tick; under B and E a small vermilion (#D55E00) cross. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Some resized copies keep the shape and some do not, even though all are rectangles.
images.description: Shows one tiger picture resized into five copies: three keep the look of the tiger, one is stretched and one is squashed.
images.context: Hook concept: images A to E measure 60 by 40, 40 by 20, 30 by 20, 90 by 60 and 60 by 60 mm.
images.teaching_notes: Ticks and crosses are symbols only, no words.

image_decisions.why: The five copies side by side pose the chapter question at a glance: what did the good copies keep?
